data.gender_notes: Maneka is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Maneka is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘mani’, which means 'jewel' or 'gem'. In Hindu mythology, Maneka is the name of a goddess associated with wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. This name is believed to bring blessings of abundance and success in life. The name Maneka carries the meaning “Jewel, Gem” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Maneka usually hope their child will grow to embody jewel, gem and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner wealth and radiance of the soul.
data.etymology: Maneka belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jewel, Gem.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maneka total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Maneka is a popular name in India, particularly in the northern states of Punjab and Haryana. It is often given to girls as a symbol of hope for a great future filled with wealth, success, and happiness. The name also reflects the cultural value of appreciating beauty and preciousness in life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Maneka is considered a divine name connected to the goddess Lakshmi, who is the deity of wealth, fortune, and prosperity. By naming a child Maneka, it is believed that the goddess bestows her blessings upon the child, ensuring their life is filled with abundance, success, and good fortune. It is a name that invokes positivity, hope, and a sense of connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Maneka: Radiant Light of the Soul. A beacon of inner illumination and transformation.

historical_references.reference: Maneka was a queen of the Mauryan Empire in the 3rd century BCE, famous for her beauty and her patronage of Jainism. She was the wife of Emperor Ashoka and is mentioned in the Ashokan inscriptions.
Maneka was a Hindu goddess, corresponding to the Greek goddess Aphrodite. She was worshipped in medieval India and was believed to bring prosperity and good fortune.
